title: Conditional Splits Breadcrumbs and Revert Wizard — UI prototype for safer rollout backtracking
creator: Lina Chen
description:
Problem: Engineers and SREs need an auditable, fast way to understand how a live split decision was reached (including conditional rules) and to perform a safe revert when metrics or signals degrade. Existing rollouts UI shows only a static traffic slider and variant list, which makes debugging multi-condition splits and partial reverts error-prone.

Goal: Design a prototype for the Console that: 1) visualizes conditional split evaluation breadcrumbs (what rules matched for a given user or request sample), 2) surfaces signal playback (time-travel) to replay why traffic moved between variants, and 3) provides a guided "Revert Wizard" that recommends the minimally disruptive rollback action (e.g., reduce % vs full revert) and shows impact estimates. The flow should be compact enough to appear inline in the rollout detail panel and also available as a modal for guided operations.

Success criteria / Acceptance criteria:
- Breadcrumb panel that shows the ordered rule evaluation chain (conditions, matched branch, sample inputs) for a selected sample or cohort.
- Signal playback timeline that overlays key metrics (latency, error rate, degenscore) and highlights the exact decision points that changed traffic composition.
- Revert Wizard that surfaces 3 recommended actions (smart-scale-down, isolate-segment, full revert) with expected immediate and 5-min impact and an audit step requiring reason + approver if > P1.
- Prototype flows in Figma with interactive hotspots and two sample playbacks (A: canary ramp anomaly, B: segmentation regression).
- Usability test with 6 engineers and 3 SREs showing median task completion time <= 4 minutes for completing a revert, and >80% confidence rating.

Design constraints and trade-offs considered:
- Keep the breadcrumbs compact — we show up to 6 rule evaluations in-line and allow expanding to full view to avoid cognitive overload on long rule chains.
- Privacy: breadcrumbs should not show raw user identifiers; we will show hashed/sample context and allow toggling anonymization for debugging sessions with elevated access.
- Automation vs manual control: Recommendations in Revert Wizard must be conservative; the default is a preview-only action requiring explicit confirmation.
- Performance: signal playback must stream lightweight aggregates; prototype uses precomputed playback slices rather than client-side heavy processing.

Accessibility notes:
- Keyboard-first navigation for the Revert Wizard steps, visible focus states for breadcrumb items, color contrast for timeline overlays, and screen-reader labels for action buttons.

Artifacts and links:
- Figma prototype: [Figma] https://www.figma.com/file/REDACTED/cond-splits-breadcrumbs-revert-wizard (interactive hotspots, two playback scenarios)
- PRD stub: https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED (context, metrics to track)
- Spike notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/REDACTED (playback data format, API contract)
- Ideas board: internal Miro: https://miro.com/app/board/REDACTED

Open questions for engineering and product:
- What is the canonical sample size we can surface in the breadcrumb panel without hitting privacy/regulatory constraints?
- Can runtime expose an "explain" endpoint returning the evaluation trace per request, and at what cost/latency?
- What guardrails are required for in-console reverts (RBAC, approval flow, mandatory audit message)?

Next steps:
- Finish high-fidelity frames for the Revert Wizard (due 2026-01-26).
- Hand off to front-end for feasibility review and a lightweight spike for the explain endpoint (assigned eng-owners listed in comments).
- Schedule a 45-minute design review with SRE and PM to align on default recommendations and approval thresholds.
